senses.sense_definition: To secretly cooperate or conspire with others to commit a wrongful, dishonest, or illegal act.

examples.text: The senior officials were accused of <w>conniving</w> with corrupt contractors to steal public funds.
Several guards decided to <w>connive</w> with the prisoners to orchestrate an escape.

senses.sense_definition: To deliberately ignore, overlook, or turn a blind eye to an immoral or illegal wrongdoing, thereby secretly encouraging or tolerating it.

examples.text: The manager chose to <w>connive</w> at his employees' dishonest behavior to meet the company targets.
Local authorities cannot afford to <w>connive</w> at safety violations in crowded public buildings.

senses.sense_definition: Of parts of a plant or organism: to converge, touch, or arch inward so as to meet at the tips.

examples.text: The upper petals of this orchid species <w>connive</w> to form a protective hood over the central reproductive organs.
Botanists noted that the delicate floral margins <w>connive</w> closely during the earliest stages of bud development.

senses.sense_definition: To open and close the eyes rapidly; to wink.

examples.text: The satirist taught the eager actor how to <w>connive</w> with an exaggerated wink on stage.
He tried to <w>connive</w> discretely to signal that the entire conversation was merely in jest.

traits.comment: Rare or archaic meaning from the Latin literal root.
